name: Arihant Superstructures Ltd
title: Arihant Superstructures Ltd - 506194 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 132 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 10 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 sales bookings were 221 units (2.31 lakh sq ft), up 15% YoY in area and value to INR 173 crore, with average realisation flat at INR 7,500 per sq ft. Consolidated operating revenue reached INR 132 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 28 crore (21% margin) and PAT INR 10 crore (7.4% margin). Net debt stood at INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore, and management reiterated plans to reduce debt from next year while funding hotel and club assets. Management guided to 2,500 unit deliveries by FY27-end and said no new land acquisitions are planned this year.

segments.name: Residential (sales)
segments.commentary: 221 units booked for 2.31 lakh sq ft at a flat average of INR 7,500 per sq ft; average ticket size about INR 78 lakh per unit. Project mix is 41% luxury per management's presentation.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Hotel at World Villas (5-star, Radisson) is concluded; second hotel near Imagicaa is in closing. Hospitality capital deployed so far is INR 35-40 crore (about 7% of capital employed of INR 730 crore), with INR 500 crore total planned over three years for hotels and club.

guidance_outlook: Deliver 2,500 units by end of FY27; expects FY27 numbers a little above FY26, but not exponential growth.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to move towards 30-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely; management said at least a 10 percentage point rise is achievable over about 12 months.
Blended PAT margin expected to exceed 20% over roughly two years.
Hotels expected to contribute INR 50 crore+ PAT per year from the third or fourth year; hospitality payback projected at 8-9 years.
Debt-to-equity expected to decline gradually as projects mature, with debt repayment focused on Arihant Advika, Vashi once cash flows allow.
Average ticket size expected to rise to INR 95 lakh-1 crore as premium mix grows; target project mix 40-45% premium, 30-35% middle income, 20% affordable.
Pre-sales convert to revenue in about 90 days on average under percentage-of-completion method.
capex_capacity: Occupancy certificates received for Arihant 5 Anaika, Arihant 6 Anaika, Arihant Anant and Arihant Aaradhya Phase 1, with about 1,495 units completed and ready for possession in coming quarters.
No new land acquisition or business development capital planned for FY27; focus on executing the INR 14,000 crore project portfolio, a 6-7 year cycle, with asset-light deals possible.
Hospitality and club program totals about INR 500 crore over three years, funded by debt or internal resources.
Average project timeline is about 4 years (range 3-5 years from start to completion).
demand_pricing: Management says demand is strongest below INR 5 crore; INR 10-30 crore tickets in Mumbai are seeing a slowdown. Overall market is normalising, with sales velocity moderate due to geopolitics, crude and FX moves, and large projects.
Navi Mumbai's share of the MMR market rose from 12% to 17% over three years, with Thane and Kalyan losing share.
Labour and skill shortages and higher construction costs are raising input costs; management says inventory on hand offsets this with no balance-sheet impact.

Blended margin fell to about 9% this quarter from 13-14% in prior years; affordable projects (below INR 5,000 per sq ft) earn single-digit to 9-10% margins, middle income up to 15%, and premium around 20% PAT.
Management is holding price rather than chasing volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of current industry volume growth is structural, and what indicators are monitored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a similar behaviour over the next four quarters and a slightly higher than last year performance, but not exponential growth this year. Indirect expenses are being held at roughly the same level.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving is captured and what further reduction is achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost reduction is not possible as HR costs are held flat year on year. Rising construction costs are offset by existing inventory, and margins should stay steady for the next three to four quarters as older projects roll off.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for converting pre-sales into revenue, given pre-sales of INR 1,731 million vs reported revenue of INR 1,316 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-sales take about 90 days on average to enter revenue recognition under percentage-of-completion, covering owner contribution, agreement, registration and NOCs.

qa_highlights.question: Are new land acquisitions attractive given higher costs?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capital investment programme for business development this year; the INR 14,000 crore project pipeline takes 6-7 years to complete. Only asset-light opportunities may be considered.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the premium share of the project mix reach, and will geography be diversified?
qa_highlights.answer: Target mix is 40-45% premium, 30-35% middle income and 20% affordable. No plans to expand to new cities; management says MMR (including Mumbai 3.0, twice the size of Mumbai city) is large enough.

qa_highlights.question: What drives average realisation, and how do margins and ROCE evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: New premium additions would raise average rates; otherwise, about 10% growth on current mix. Margins are expected to rise toward 30-35% EBITDA with villa projects; ROCE is said to be on an increasing trajectory on a project basis. Capital employed of INR 730 crore is 90-93% residential.

risks_watch: Blended margin compression: the quarter's blended margin fell to about 9% from 13-14% in prior years, and management's margin recovery depends on villa and premium projects ramping up.
Net debt of INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore; debt reduction depends on completions at Arihant Advika, Vashi, offset by new loans for hotels and club.
Rising construction and labour costs from geopolitical factors and labour shortages; management says inventory offsets this, but no quantification was given.
Sales slowdown above INR 10 crore ticket sizes in Mumbai and moderating market velocity.
Concentration in MMR with no geographic diversification; hospitality execution and operator tie-ups are still ahead.
Management claims of 'no competition' for large hotels in Lonavala, Karjat and Mumbai and of 30-35% EBITDA margins are forward-looking and unquantified in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand in MMR and project completions, and on margin recovery, but cautious on volume growth ("very exponential growth ... will not be able to witness in this financial year"). Answers on margin and debt timelines were vague and several were given as 'can be' or 'expected' without figures.
key_quotes: We plan to deliver 2,500 units by the end of financial year 2027.
Our average selling price per square feet has also remained same at INR 7,500 per square feet which is almost similar to Q1FY26.

We remain focused and confident on reducing our debt next year onwards as some of our residential projects have started nearing completion and these reductions will be partially offset by new loans which are being taken for building the annuity assets.
Going forward for this financial year, we don't have any program for new capital investments for the business development as there is a good handsome size of projects in hand worth INR 14,000 crores

adds.what: Hotel at World Villas (5-star, Radisson) concluded; second hotel near Imagicaa in closing (hospitality, not residential production capacity)
About 1,495 completed units across Arihant 5 Anaika, Arihant 6 Anaika, Arihant Anant and Arihant Aaradhya Phase 1 ready for possession (OCs received)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 numbers a little above FY26 with 2,500 unit deliveries by FY27-end, backed by about 1,495 completed units ready for possession and pre-sales converting to revenue in about 90 days, while sales bookings rose 15% YoY in area; no new land is planned and blended margin fell to about 9%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters for stabilisation; villa-led recovery over
rows.why: Blended margin fell to about 9% from 13-14% prior years and EBITDA margin is 21% this quarter, with management guiding 30-35% only once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely, and offsetting cost inflation with existing inventory but no quantification.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 to Q2 FY27 (ready-for-possession units in coming qua
rows.why: OCs received for Arihant 5 Anaika, 6 Anaika, Anant and Aaradhya Phase 1 with about 1,495 units completed and ready for possession, supporting the 2,500 unit delivery target by FY27-end; this is completed inventory rather than new production capacity, and no new land is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 full year, a little above FY26
rows.why: Sales bookings rose 15% YoY in area to 2.31 lakh sq ft (221 units), but management explicitly ruled out exponential growth and expects only slightly higher performance than last year, with Mumbai INR 10-30 crore tickets slowing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new land or business development capital planned for FY27, but INR 500 crore hospitality and club programme over three years is funded by debt or internal resources, with INR 35-40 crore deployed so far (about 7% of INR 730 crore capital employed); the hotel near Imagicaa is in closing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 only a little above FY26 with no exponential growth, and is holding price rather than chasing volume amid a moderating market.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Blended margin already fell to about 9% from 13-14%, net debt is INR 818 crore against net worth of INR 460 crore, and construction and labour cost inflation is unquantified, with the margin recovery reliant on villa projects ramping.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Town Villas and villa projects are cited as the main margin driver, and the hotel near Imagicaa is in closing, though no specific launch dates or unit counts were given.

rows.label: Debt reduction from next year (Arihant Advika, Vashi completions)
rows.when: from FY28, depending on cash flows
rows.why: Net debt is INR 818 crore against INR 460 crore net worth, and management's repayment plan is vague and conditional on completions, offset by new hotel and club borrowings.

rows.label: Average ticket size rise to INR 95 lakh-1 crore via premium mix
rows.why: Current ticket is about INR 78 lakh at a flat INR 7,500 per sq ft realisation; the target rise depends on premium additions (target 40-45% premium mix), which is not yet quantified.

rows.label: Pre-sales conversion to revenue in about 90 days
rows.why: Pre-sales of INR 1,731 million against reported revenue of INR 1,316 million indicate about INR 415 million of bookings still to convert to revenue under percentage-of-completion.

tone.note: Management was confident on MMR demand, completions and margin recovery through villa projects, but cautious on volume with no exponential growth this year; analysts pushed on the margin drop to 9%, debt reduction timing and cost inflation, and answers were vague with few figures.
